FluvialGeomorph supports repeatable analysis of stream geometry from remotely
sensed terrain, especially lidar. Its shared methods and reports help analysts
describe channels through maps, longitudinal comparisons, cross-section metrics
and profiles. **FG Studio is the developing browser workspace that brings the
early decisions and data preparation for that work into a coherent, reviewable
study.** Its longer-term destination is a guided route to Level 1 analysis and
scientific deliverables using the project's shared R backend.

## Why the study comes before the analysis

A terrain file alone does not explain a study. An analyst needs to know which
question it serves, what area and stream corridor it represents, how Reaches were
defined, when observations were acquired, and which reference systems and units
make comparisons meaningful. These choices influence every later calculation.

Historically, preparing those inputs has depended on highly trained GIS analysts
and knowledge that can be difficult to transfer. FG Studio aims to make the work
understandable and repeatable through visual feedback, explicit choices and a
retained study record. Scientific judgment remains essential: discovering a
dataset, downloading it or selecting a CRS does not establish its fitness for
an engineering question.

For example, a team assessing a stream corridor can define the Study Area and
Reaches, inspect available lidar acquisitions, retain original DEM tiles and
record intended reference systems today. The next terrain steps will organize
those acquisitions into Survey Events and produce consistently aligned terrain.
The intended continuation is shared analysis and reports that another analyst
or customer can review without reconstructing the originating GIS session.

## Where it fits in the workspace

The project consists of independently maintained repositories. They have different
responsibilities; an implemented backend function is not automatically an exposed
FG Studio feature.

| Component | Role and relationship to FG Studio |
| --- | --- |
| **fgstudio** | Shiny interaction, reactive state, review of choices and orchestration of local saved studies |
| **fluvgeo** | Shared R scientific calculations, spatial contracts and validation, plots and reporting; FG Studio delegates reusable methods here |
| **fg-qgis-toolbox** | Developing desktop access to shared R capabilities; interaction is designed alongside Shiny, with its own qualification and rollout |
| **FluvialGeomorph-toolbox** | Established ArcGIS/Python orchestration; ongoing production workflows are retained during the open-source transition |
| **ohwm2** | An existing Shiny client and interaction reference; FG Studio has its own repository and workflow |
| **FGDB** | Governed study identities, relationships, validation and enterprise-loading contracts; future integration is distinct from today's local saves |
| **RegionalCurve / fluvgeodata** | Regional hydraulic geometry capabilities and backend test/example fixtures, respectively |
| **FG-User-Manual / FG-Tech-Manual** | Project-wide user procedures and technical methods; prototype app guidance does not replace established production instructions |
| **FG-architecture** | Cross-repository context, ownership and accepted architectural decisions; member repositories retain implementation authority |

The accepted design starts with Shiny's new-project experience and develops shared
capabilities toward a verified connection with existing FluvialGeomorph tools.
QGIS offers desktop control over those capabilities. Client screens need not map
one-to-one to backend functions. This approach supports an open-source, R-native
workflow while preserving the existing production toolchain.

Within that workflow, vector work uses **sf** and raster work uses **terra** in
the shared backend. CRS handling follows their geospatial libraries rather than
an independent app projection engine. The planned NSRS transition makes explicit
reference frames, coordinate epochs, vertical references and exact units especially
important. Present metadata support is preparation for qualified operations,
not a claim of complete NATRF2022/NAPGD2022/SPCS2022 processing support.

## The workflow and its current boundary

The intended progression is **study question → study definition → terrain
development → analysis → reviewable results**. Analysts may revisit earlier
choices as scope and evidence develop; this is not a rigid wizard.

| Stage | Useful result | Current FG Studio support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Define the study | Named Study Area with purpose, boundary, Streams and Reaches | Implemented, with local immutable revisions and supported hierarchy editing |
| Find and inspect observations | Retained acquisition choices, original DEMs and evidence about their contents | Survey Collection discovery, DEM selection/download and bounded inspection implemented |
| Specify analysis references | Explicit horizontal and vertical targets and units | Implemented as checked, saved specifications; no elevation conversion on save |
| Develop analysis terrain | One consistent Stream DEM per Survey Event, aligned grids and hierarchical masks | Planned; Event membership, explicit cell size, source reconciliation and processing remain to be implemented |
| Analyze and report | Reach-level geometry evidence and a reviewable explanation of the study and its terrain | Shared backend capabilities and reporting designs inform the destination; app execution/report delivery remain future work |
| Govern and share accepted content | Qualified enterprise records and relationships | Eventual FGDB integration; no Enterprise connection in this app |

The current app is a local preview for a trusted single analyst. It is useful for
the implemented preparation tasks, but is not yet a complete Level 1 execution
environment or a shared hosted service. The [analyst guide](guide-study-workflow.html)
describes current buttons, persistence and operational limits.

## A durable record across clients and time

Study Area, Stream and Reach definitions provide the spatial context for Survey
Events and their products. An app **Survey Collection** is source-acquisition
evidence; it is not an FGDB **Collection**, which groups Study Areas, nor is
selecting it the creation of a Survey Event. Event identity and membership need
their own explicit handling.

The accepted local delivery direction uses GeoPackages for vectors/tables,
external GeoTIFFs for analytical terrain, and links and metadata within a related
folder. FG Studio already retains context revisions, source selections and
download evidence locally. That does not yet constitute a fully qualified
analysis-delivery bundle or an enterprise-accepted dataset. Back up the entire
study folder; the newest context alone is not all the evidence.

The wider project also supports a separate entry problem: reconstructing legacy
studies from surviving archives. New-project design and legacy reconstruction
should describe the same scientific relationships, but have different evidence
and uncertainty. FG Studio currently emphasizes new-study definition; it is not
an archive migration tool. The broader reporting intent distinguishes Study Area,
Terrain Development and staging views without making four separate documents
mandatory for every user.

## Why this site also documents development

The app is both a user workflow under development and a practical setting for
testing human/agent context routing. These purposes share an implementation, but
have distinct evidence: application tests check behavior; navigation experiments
ask whether a maintainer can find and explain that behavior accurately and with
less effort.

The analyst guide describes tasks and outcomes. Developer articles trace events,
state, adapters, shared backend calls, failures and tests. Agent routes provide a
short entry to the same sources; generated maps help answer bounded dependency
questions. The [methods article](dev-01-code-navigation.html) records the first
pilot's limits and the evidence needed before claiming efficiency gains.
Neither an AI account nor an agent is required to use or maintain the application.

## Further reading and authority

This orientation synthesizes the maintained workspace context reviewed on
2026-09-20. Current app behavior comes from fgstudio's implementation and tests;
the following documents explain the wider purpose and accepted direction.
Their member repositories own changes to those contracts.

- [Shiny-led new-project design](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/FG-architecture/blob/main/dev/decisions/adr-0008-shiny-led-new-project-design.md): browser/desktop roles and staged convergence.
- [Shared reporting intent](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/fluvgeo/blob/main/dev/goals/reporting-intent.md): the scientific record, accessibility and new-study versus legacy-study distinction.
- [Backend ecosystem](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/fluvgeo/blob/main/dev/architecture/backend-ecosystem.md): scientific ownership, client responsibilities and compatibility.
- [FGDB initiative](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/FGDB/blob/main/dev/goals/initiative-brief.md): governed relationships and enterprise goals.
- [QGIS toolbox](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/fg-qgis-toolbox): the parallel desktop development path.
- [User Manual](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/FG-User-Manual) and [Technical Manual](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/FG-Tech-Manual): project procedures and methods.
- [Deterministic user tooling](https://github.com/FluvialGeomorph/FG-architecture/blob/main/dev/decisions/adr-0006-deterministic-user-tooling.md): separation of AI-assisted development from runtime requirements.

Repository links refer to published copies and may lag local development changes.
In a workspace checkout, read the same repository-relative paths for current
evidence; this site does not publish or synchronize sibling repositories.
